Southeast Michigan will reside on the northern periphery of a high 
pressure ridge slowly migrating east across the OH/TN Valleys to the 
Atlantic Coast over the next several days. A warm and humid airmass 
will settle into the area and persist and support chances for 
multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms with some storms 
possibly becoming strong to severe. Models struggling to come to a 
consensus with this pattern and predictability remains low over the 
next 2-3 days.

For today, an 850-500 mb theta-e ridge axis containing deep moisture
will hover around lower Michigan today and pivot northward later in 
the day. Surface dewpoints have already climbed to the 70 marks in 
parts of the area this morning. The 00Z RAOB from last evening 
observed PWAT at 1.60 inches with PWATS approaching 2.00 inches 
expected to pivot northward with the theta-e ridge. Temperatures at 
850 mb have also climbed to 20C and are forecast to hold around there
over the next couple days, which would support high temperatures up 
to around 90 degrees. Presence of a cap with warming mid-levels along
with some drying aloft is bringing some confidence that any 
widespread convection is becoming less likely today. This leans the 
forecast towards the higher temperature outcome putting heat indices 
up toward 100 degrees in parts of Lower Michigan. It still looks 
borderline for prolonged heat indices to 100 degrees or greater, so 
will hold off on any headlines for now. Regardless, a warm and muggy 
day will be in store. While widespread convection looks unlikely 
during much of the day, the underlying environment will be supportive
of strong to severe thunderstorms if any cells are able to overcome 
any capping via local boundaries. SBCAPE values will be up to 2000+ 
J/kg with the NAM advertising 4000-5000 j/kg by late afternoon. 
Effective shear will be up to 40+ knots and mid-level lapse rates 
will be up to 6-7 C/km. Late this afternoon into the early half of 
tonight appears to be the best opportunity for potential convection 
to develop while a shortwave also rounds the ridge across Lake 
Michigan. Confidence remains low on where convection may develop, but
the parts of the Saginaw Valley close to Saginaw Bay looks favored 
by some of the latest guidance. Will also need to keep an eye on any
upstream development that may try and roll into the forecast area. 
Any cells or clusters of cells that can develop will be capable of 
strong to severe winds and hail along with heavy downpours that could
lead to localized flooding, thus the entire CWA is in a Marginal 
Risk for severe weather. 

For tomorrow, a shortwave within a belt of strong mid-level westerly 
along with a potential nearby cold frontal boundary will be the 
items of interest for another round of potential strong to severe 
thunderstorm development. Models again not offering much consensus 
on how Wednesday may play out, as some point to an early afternoon 
uptick in convection while others point toward convection not 
occuring until late in the day into Wednesday night. Timing of 
convection ultimately will determine overall severe weather threat. 
Parameter space though bulk of the day will again be supportive of 
isolated to scattered severe weather if timed well in the diurnal 
cycle (MLCAPEs to 1000-3000 J/kg, effective shear to 40+ knots, and 
mid-level lapse rates 6-7 C/km). Severe wind and hail with locally 
heavy rain will again be the main threats with a low end tornado 
potential. The other item of note for Wednesday will be the heat and 
humidity bringing heat index values back up to around 100 degrees, 
which will be dependent on how convection eventually plays out. 
Headlines may be possible if early day convection does not pan out 
and less cloud cover allows for max heat index values to be realized.

Aforementioned cold front will eventually be pushed southward 
keeping shower and thunderstorm chances in the forecast late 
Wednesday night into Thursday morning. Though, instability will be 
decreasing throughout the night. The frontal boundary hanging around 
lower Michigan Thursday morning/afternoon will again provide a focus 
for additional isolated strong to possibly severe convection as 
another shortwave is advertised to crest the building ridge axis. 
Post frontal airmass does look to cool daytime temperatures back 
down into the 80s for the late week period.
